observation_summary: The DateTimeFormatter.parseInto method incorrectly resets the year of the target instant to a default value (2000) when parsing partial dates, leading to incorrect date results.
hypothesis: The DateTimeFormatter.parseInto method incorrectly uses a hardcoded default year (iDefaultYear) when parsing date strings that lack year information, instead of using the year from the provided instant.
prediction: The DateTimeParserBucket constructor in DateTimeFormatter is being initialized with iDefaultYear, which overrides the existing year in the target instant. Changing this to use the year from the instant itself will resolve the issue.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and the provided fix diff clearly indicate that the initialization of the DateTimeParserBucket was using an incorrect default value instead of the current instant's year.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the initialization of the DateTimeParserBucket to use 'chrono.year().get(instantLocal)' instead of 'iDefaultYear'. This is a classic case of incorrect initialization of a state variable during a parsing operation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a flaw in the parsing algorithm itself, but rather the incorrect initialization of the context (bucket) used by the algorithm.
There is no missing guard or predicate; the logic is simply using the wrong value for initialization.
